Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.

"Scans at the Clive Berghofer Centre’s Qscan facility confirmed that Broncos captain Adam Reynolds sustained a grade 1 soleus strain on his right calf at training yesterday," the club said.

'Sky is still the limit': Koula's added motivation as Manly fight for finals
The Sea Eagles are determined to ensure their season comes full circle when they host the Dolphins in a must-win clash on Friday night.
Manly kicked off the Fozball era with a thumping 52-18 win over the Dolphins in Round 5 but they have struggled in recent weeks.
Five-straight losses have left Manly sitting 10th on the ladder, four points outside the top eight with just four games remaining.
Dolphins v Sea Eagles – Round 5, 2026
Standing in their way this weekend are the fifth-placed Dolphins, with Manly needing a win to keep pace in a congested finals race.
“We still have a chance for finals, and hopefully we chase that this weekend, get a win and turn it around,” Haumole Olakau’atu said.
“The last couple of weeks haven’t been the best for us.
“It comes down to our attitude, our mindset and turning up on the day and playing for each other.”

There is a sense of deja vu about Friday night.
The last time Manly faced the Dolphins, Foran had just taken over as interim coach in Round Five, sparking a four-game winning streak that ignited the Sea Eagles' season.
With Foran now permanently in charge, Manly are hoping to produce another turnaround against the same opponent, this time with their season hanging in the balance.
“We’ve had glimpses in the last couple of weeks, the results haven’t gone our way,” halfback Jamal Fogarty said.
“Foz is giving us game plans, giving us confidence and belief.”
The players have continued to back Foran through the difficult run, with Fogarty adamant the responsibility sits with the playing group to turn their form around.
Haumole looking ominous early
“It’s us as a team, us as players and the club,” he said.
“Foz is doing a wonderful job.
“We know what we are playing for. We try to go out there every single week to get a win and perform well and some weeks that doesn’t happen.
“If we have 17 guys do that on the weekend, we’ll get a result.”
Friday night will also carry a different kind of significance for centre Tolu Koula.
The 24-year-old will run out for his 100th NRL game, a milestone that brings his career full circle, with Foran and Olakau’atu both alongside him when he made his first-grade debut for Manly in 2022.
“It was always a dream of mine to make my NRL debut,” Koula said.
“It feels like a little while now. I remember coming on at left centre and Foz was the half.
“It’s crazy now that he’s my coach.
“Haumole was in the team as well and a few of the other boys.”
Koula has the need... the need for speed
Olakau’atu still remembers the teenager who nervously made his way around the sidelines before getting his chance.
“It’s a very special round for him and his family,” Olakau’atu said.
“I still remember his first game.
“I remember a young, shy kid walking up and down the sidelines, getting ready to jump on.
“We all know how explosive and fast he is, he played really well that night.
“We all know how good he’s been for the past 99 games. The sky is still the limit for him.
“He’s a very good player, and I can’t wait for what the future holds for him.”
Koula has since developed into one of Manly’s most dangerous attacking weapons, earning a NSW debut this season and establishing himself as a key part of the Sea Eagles’ future.
But his 100th game will mean little if Manly cannot keep their season alive.
Four games remain, and with every point crucial in the race for the top eight, Friday night shapes as a must-win for Foran’s side.

NRL teams Round 24: Raiders coach Ricky Stuart axes Corey Horsburgh
Ricky Stuart has sensationally swung the axe on a Raiders star after his ‘brain explosion’, while an exiled star has moved one step closer to an NRL return. See all the Round 24 teams news.
Fiery Canberra forward Corey Horsburgh has been dramatically dropped for Saturday’s away game against Cronulla at Ocean Protect Stadium.
The Raiders claim Horsburgh has been rested after a controversial performance against Newcastle last weekend.
Horsburgh won’t play NSW Cup this weekend.
Ata Mariota will be Horsburgh’s replacement at starting prop against the Sharks.
It is unknown whether Horsburgh will be considered for NRL selection in Canberra’s round 25 game against Brisbane.
Horsburgh’s omission is another clear sign that he and the club are at loggerheads.
Others you may like
Corey Horsburgh has been dropped by the Raiders ahead of their clash against the Sharks. Picture: Getty Images
His demise is the culmination of a difficult week after Horsburgh drew sharp criticism for a “brain explosion” at a pivotal moment in Canberra’s loss to the Knights.
Horsburgh was sin binned for slapping opponent Dane Gagai nearing fulltime in the Raiders’ 30-24 loss, which ended the club’s finals hopes.
Stuart singled out Horsburgh for criticism at a post-match press conference.
“It was a f***ing brain explosion and (we) lost the opportunity,” Stuart fumed.
The pair have been getting along well in recent times while enjoying or enduring a rollercoaster relationship over the past eight years.
Corey Horsburgh has been dropped by the Raiders ahead of their clash against the Sharks. Picture: Getty Images. Picture: NRL Photos
This masthead can confirm that Canberra would be prepared to offload Horsburgh early if he can secure another NRL club.
A former Queensland State of Origin player, Horsburgh comes off contract at Canberra after next season.
Caboolture-born Horsburgh, 28, would prefer a return to Queensland but Perth is also monitoring the situation.
The Bears are also ready to make a move on Horsburgh.
Brisbane has been gently linked to Horsburgh but the Broncos’ star-studded roster may prevent an offer being lodged.
But there was speculation on Tuesday that Horsburgh could join Brisbane as early as next season.
Ill-discipline has cost Canberra this season with last year’s minor premiers sitting in the 12th spot with nine wins from 21 games.
Canberra’s finals round games are against Cronulla, Brisbane and North Queensland.
—Dean Ritchie
EXILED STAR ONE STEP CLOSER TO NRL RETURN
—Tyson Jackson
Former Manly star Josh Schuster has been handed his first opportunity with new club the Wests Tigers, named to play five-eighth with the club’s NSW Cup team on Sunday.
Schuster, who has spent the last couple of months training with the Tigers reserve grade squad, will finally get his opportunity to play alongside Javon Andrews, as he tries to get his NRL career back on track.
Josh Schuster has been named to play five-eighth for the Wests Tigers’ NSW Cup team. Picture: Instagram
The former Sea Eagle and Rabbitoh took a train and trial deal with the Tigers until the end of the year, with the club wanting to help Schuster get back to the NRL.
It’s understood the five-eighth has lost a lot of weight and has impressed the Tigers in his couple of months training.
Schuster was initially not expected to get a game with the club before next year, but will now have the opportunity to play for a new contract this Sunday.
